The boundary registry and the target platform layer stay small and enumerable enough that one person can read the entire trusted base in an afternoon and know what they are trusting.

```day-telos
{"witnesses":["trusted-base-inventory"]}
```

---

Unchanged, which for this telos is the intended outcome. The registry is still 104 operations over 12 domains and 19 capability kinds, and the platform layer is 12 files forked byte-identical to the pin bar one declared divergence. Nothing this pass added a registry entry or a platform path. The Containerfile enlarges the build-time trusted base by one pinned image digest, which is a real addition and is recorded on every published artifact rather than left implicit.

  "text_len": 389,
  "content": ""

---

Bulla's verified core performs no privileged operations. It computes (State, Action) pairs where an action describes an effect; a shell outside interprets the alphabet and performs them. #[boundary] does not appear in the core. Derived from the meso choice: boundaries make the trusted base grow at the same rate as the verified core, which is what readable-trusted-base exists to prevent.
